entities.summary: Erywan bin Haji Mohd. Yusof is the incumbent 2nd Minister of Foreign Affairs of Brunei, a position he has held since 2018. He previously served as ASEAN's first special envoy to Myanmar from August to December 2021, following the Myanmar coup d'état and the resulting civil war. Born in the 1960s, Yusof's early life and education are not well-documented, but he has been a prominent figure in Bruneian politics for over two decades. As a member of the ruling Party of Progressiveness, Yusof has been instrumental in shaping Brunei's foreign policy and strengthening its relationships with Southeast Asian nations. His tenure as foreign minister has been marked by significant efforts to promote regional stability and counter China's growing influence in the region. Despite criticisms of Brunei's human rights record, Yusof has remained a key figure in regional diplomacy, working closely with ASEAN leaders to address common challenges. Yusof's legacy is complex, with some hailing him as a shrewd politician and others criticizing his role in maintaining Brunei's authoritarian regime. As the country continues to navigate the challenges of the post-pandemic era, Yusof's leadership will be closely watched by regional observers.
